clue.text: Villain about to mug man or woman outside rear of café

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the name sits outside, wrapping around, the word for mugging

parts.note: Pat is a first name given to both men and women
to mug someone is to rob them

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, here taken from café

explanation.surface: A villain is about to attack a passer-by just outside the back of a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man or woman' needs a name that suits either sex: PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, a fair synonym for a villain.

clue.text: He may make bloomers, needing the dough, so to speak

definitions.text: He may make bloomers, needing the dough, so to speak

parts.words: He may make bloomers, needing the dough, so to speak
parts.note: bloomers here are crusty loaves rather than blunders or underwear, and 'needing' said out loud is 'kneading', which is what one does to dough when making bread

explanation.surface: Someone prone to embarrassing blunders who is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' flags the pun: 'needing' sounds like 'kneading'. A bloomer is a British loaf with diagonal slashes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread maker produces bloomer loaves and kneads dough as part of the trade.

clue.text: Tell untruths for example about feudal lord

parts.note: to tell untruths is to lie

indicators.note: about here signals turning the abbreviation round so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone lies, for instance, about the local nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal society a liege was the lord to whom a vassal owed allegiance.

clue.text: Eccentric character on staff possibly, one manipulating clubs?

parts.note: a card is an old-fashioned word for an amusing oddball
a sharp sign is written on the musical staff (stave) to raise a note

explanation.surface: An odd member of the workforce who wields golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is the five-line musical staff; 'clubs' is the card suit, not golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp cheats at cards, manipulating the deck including the suit of clubs.

clue.text: Family touring brash, crazy duke's fantasy world

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the family word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group
loud can mean brash or showy
cuckoo is slang for crazy
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A clan travelling with a loud mad aristocrat in his dream realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an idiom for an unrealistic fantasy world, from Aristophanes' The Birds.

clue.text: Bogus power source English moved to front? Scandalous!

parts.note: a sham is something bogus or fake

indicators.note: the letter for English is taken from its place and shifted to the start of the fuel word

parts.note: fuel is a source of power

explanation.surface: Outrage at a fake energy supply rearranged by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved to front' carries the E of FUEL to its start, giving EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful and scandalous both describe conduct that brings disgrace.

clue.text: Part of the head's place of worship

definitions.meaning: the flat area at each side of the forehead
a building for religious worship, as in Hindu or Jewish faiths

explanation.surface: Somebody's head contains a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the side of the forehead and a building devoted to worship.

clue.text: Sally's vessel used in distilling

definitions.meaning: a sally is a witty riposte or quick comeback
a glass flask with a long downward-bent neck used by chemists for distillation

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally owns a still.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sharp reply and a long-necked laboratory flask for distilling.

clue.text: Travelled in formal wear for ten years

indicators.note: the travelling word is placed inside the neckwear word

parts.note: ties are worn with formal dress
went is the past of go, to travel

explanation.surface: Someone went about in a suit and tie for a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are a decade, the ten years of a century numbered twenty to twenty-nine.

clue.text: Like some fat aunts cavorting in college for all to see?

indicators.note: the jumbled relatives go inside the college-and-certificate pieces

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a former type of British college
U-rated is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters of aunts are jumbled

explanation.surface: Plump aunts frolicking at a college in public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but places the jumble inside: U-rated is the UK film certificate for universal viewing, POLY a former British polytechnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyunsaturated fats have several double bonds; the term describes a class of dietary fat.

clue.text: Around Christmas, drink brought about one's initial impropriety

indicators.note: the drink is brought round to come after the letter from one's, reversing the clue's order

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec, so around then is 'in Dec'

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here of one's

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Getting drunk over the festive season led to someone's first lapse in decorum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' swaps the order, putting the O from 'one's initial' before RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, so it serves as a synonym for impropriety.

clue.text: Mature northern actor's third character in rep?

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: the third letter of the word actor's is wanted

explanation.surface: An ageing northern actor playing a role in repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' looks like repertory theatre but is a sales representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep, short for representative, is someone acting for a company, i.e. its agent.

clue.text: Mawkish attempt to invite intimacy at last?

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: at last tells us to take the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A sentimental try at getting close to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooey can mean sickly sentimental, which is what mawkish describes.

clue.text: Gloat over woman losing husband in city

indicators.note: over signals that the gloating word is turned back to front

parts.note: to crow is to gloat

indicators.note: losing means the letter for husband drops out of the name

parts.note: Esther is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone gloats over a widowed woman in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the gloating word; Worcester is an English cathedral city, home of the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is a cathedral city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Surviving artefact held by Grasmere licensee

indicators.note: the run of letters is held within the words Grasmere licensee

explanation.surface: An old object kept by a pub landlord in a Lake District village.
explanation.walkthrough: Grasmere is a village in the English Lake District; a licensee runs a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object that survives from an earlier time.

clue.text: A pretty cold, curious old flying reptile

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so these letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: A cute little chill, oddly linked to a prehistoric flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterodactyls were winged reptiles of the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.

clue.text: Late priest set up in love directly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the priest's title is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title
due means directly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A clergyman put into romance straight away arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; VER is REV turned by 'set up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past the expected time.

clue.text: Star manoeuvring cart before game in America

indicators.note: before in a down clue puts the rearranged cart above the following pieces
manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters of cart are rearranged
in means the game's letters sit inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the United States
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A celebrity steering a cart ahead of a match in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCT is the anagram of CART from 'manoeuvring'; RU (rugby union) goes 'in' US.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes.

clue.text: I've found it, giving rise to regret over 7, oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece
in a down clue, rising means the word for regret is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: oddly signals that the letters of the referenced answer are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is the parrot name KEA

explanation.surface: A discovery that makes someone regret something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: EUR is RUE reversed by 'giving rise to'; 'oddly' turns KEA into EKA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka is Greek for 'I have found it', Archimedes' cry of discovery.

clue.text: Made to order half of beer at bar

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word beer is its first two letters

parts.note: a spoke is a bar or rod in a wheel

explanation.surface: Someone orders a half of beer at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke means made to a customer's order, as with tailoring.

clue.text: Parrot a romantic poet, ignoring Eliot initially

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the poet's name drops the letters
initially here points to the poet's initials rather than the first letter of his surname

parts.note: John Keats was an English Romantic poet
the poet T. S. Eliot is known by his initials T and S

explanation.surface: A bird imitating a Romantic poet but not Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' means Eliot's initials, TS, not the E of Eliot; 'ignoring' drops them from KEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a large mountain parrot of New Zealand.

clue.text: Speed paras' leader adopted in assault on headland

indicators.note: the letter is taken into the middle of the assault word

parts.note: a raid is a sudden assault

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, from paras'

parts.note: ness is a headland, common in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Parachute troops rushing an attack on a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link joining the pieces; NESS appears in place names like Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is quickness, the state of having speed.

clue.text: Post a very soft embrocation

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
an embrocation is a liniment or ointment rubbed on the body

explanation.surface: Mail a very gentle rub-on cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a verb about mail but means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A post, as in a job, is also called an appointment.

clue.text: Youngster needing member's support to cover outing

indicators.note: the sling wraps round and covers the outing word

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm, a limb or member
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A child with an arm in a sling for a day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man, a youngster not yet fully grown.

clue.text: One's disloyal to date another finally, taking in wife

indicators.note: the pieces take in, contain, the letter for wife

parts.note: a date is a particular time

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of another

explanation.surface: Someone cheating by going out with someone else while married.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is someone unfaithful, deceiving a partner by seeing another.

clue.text: Lewd bloke eating meal left out

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the name surrounds the meal word

parts.note: Ray is a man's name, so stands for a bloke

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed from the meal

parts.note: lunch is a meal

explanation.surface: A crude fellow wolfing down food, leaving bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' with 'left' drops the L from the meal; 'bloke' needs a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy means sexually explicit or coarse, near to lewd.

clue.text: Tell heartless tale following overthrow of island

indicators.note: following puts the next piece after the island name
overthrow means turning over, so the island's name is reversed

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of tale are removed

explanation.surface: Recount a gutted story about an island's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow of' reverses ARRAN to NARRA; 'heartless' leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story.

clue.text: Key argument for conditional execution of deed

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A crucial dispute over carrying out a deed under conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Escrow holds a deed with a third party until conditions are met, then it takes effect.

clue.text: Discourage browsers? About time

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the animal word goes around the time letter

parts.note: deer browse, nibbling leaves and shoots

explanation.surface: Put off people looking in shops, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browsers' suggests shoppers or web software, but means grazing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting.

clue.text: Fleece worn by university couple?

indicators.note: worn by means held inside, so the university letter goes inside

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or fleece them

explanation.surface: A fleece jacket worn by a university student and partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, a couple of people acting together.
